facts.statement: A feature for a prediction must be derived only from information available when that prediction is made.
A list comprehension of the form [row for row in records if row["available_at"] <= prediction_time] selects the records available at the declared boundary.
A changing lookup table can yield different training and serving values, so use values from the relevant recorded boundary rather than assuming the latest table is historical.
Test the feature on the original records and on records augmented with later unavailable observations, asserting that the earlier feature is unchanged.
Apply the declared arithmetic feature to the time-filtered records only; for a sum, initialize total = 0 and accumulate total += record["value"] over the accepted list.

practice.objective: Implement a learner-defined Python function that accepts records and prediction_time, filters records with a list comprehension using available_at <= prediction_time, and sums only accepted value entries. Write the required datetime import for the supplied timestamp fixtures. Within the supplied infrastructure scaffolding, author assertions and verify the function with supplied unit-test fixtures, including a record exactly at the boundary and an added later observation.
practice.success: The available values 2 and 3 produce 5. Adding the later value 7 leaves the earlier feature at 5. A record exactly at prediction_time is included, and the learner-written assertions and supplied feature fixtures pass.

live_code.required_skill: Write a function that filters timestamped records before arithmetic and asserts that later unavailable records cannot change its result.
allowed_syntax: dictionary literals with available_at and value keys
[row for row in records if row["available_at"] <= prediction_time]
live_code.starter_state_intent: Supply an authorized harness, an unimplemented feature-function interface, and timestamp fixtures using only records, prediction_time, available_at, and value. Include available values 2 and 3, a later value 7, and an exact-boundary case. Leave the import, function implementation, and invariance assertions for the learner.
live_code.observable_success: The function returns 5 for the original records and for records augmented with the later value 7. Learner-written assertions confirm equality of those results, and supplied fixtures confirm inclusion at the exact boundary and exclusion after it.
